note: Files in scripts/ci/ that scripts/ci/run-guards.sh deliberately does NOT run. 'exempt' means the file runs nowhere at all; 'own_step' means a workflow invokes it directly because the runner cannot give it what it needs. scripts/ci/guard-registry-check.py fails the build when a file is in neither section nor in the runner's discovered set, when an entry has an empty reason, when an entry names a file that no longer exists, when an 'exempt' file turns out to be wired to a workflow after all, and when an 'own_step' file is referenced by no workflow. Every reason has to be checkable by a reviewer — 'not a guard' is not a reason.

exempt.clean-install-check.sh: Local-only developer tool (D#1617, PR #1623): it builds a throwaway venv on a dev host to reproduce what CI already does. The backend (import-smoke) job IS that clean install — it pip-installs only requirements.txt onto a fresh runner and then runs the same scripts/ci/backend-import-smoke.py — so as a CI step this would nest a venv inside an already-clean runner and add the get-pip.py network fetch its ensurepip fallback makes, which nothing else in this workflow needs.

own_step.backend-import-smoke.py: The job's namesake and the precondition for everything the runner runs after it: every Python guard imports backend modules, so a broken import has to be reported as one import failure rather than as every guard failing at once. Runs as its own step in backend (import-smoke), before the runner.
own_step.guard-registry-check.py: Runs as its own step in backend (import-smoke) under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, so it still reports when the runner step before it goes red. Inside the runner it could say nothing about a runner that failed to start — which is the one condition that would hide every guard at once.
own_step.pr-link-policy.sh: Runs in pr-gates.yml's `PR body link policy` job. It reads the PR body out of $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH into a PR_BODY_FILE the step writes first; there is no PR event payload in backend (import-smoke), and pr-gates.yml also needs the `edited` trigger so an edited body is re-checked.
own_step.publish-denylist.sh: Runs in pr-gates.yml's `publish denylist` job. It three-dot-diffs the PR head against PUBLISH_DENYLIST_BASE from the PR event and needs `fetch-depth: 0` for a real merge base in the object store; backend (import-smoke) checks out shallow and has neither.
